set_d.instruction: Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below.
set_d.passage:
Following Tuesday’s talks between the Special Representatives (SRs) on the boundary question , India and China have agreed to substantial outcomes on managing the disputed border . According to an eight-point consensus released on Wednesday, both countries have agreed to advance discussions on “an early and substantial harvest of boundary delimitation”. They have agreed to hold next month a meeting of an expert-level mechanism on trans-border rivers and to maintain communication on sharing hydrological data, which India has been pushing for. Two additional meeting points to hold talks between top military commanders will be set up, along with two new channels of hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi reaffirmed the efforts taken over the past two years to keep the peace along the Line of Actual Control, and committed to continuing the on-going normalisation in relations. That the NSA’s visit to Beijing took place before India hosts the BRICS Summit, on September 12, underlined both sides’ keenness to continue with this process of re-engagement, with the expected visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping after a gap of seven years. An October 2024 meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Xi kickstarted this calibrated effort towards normalcy, and a 2025 meeting in Tianjin helped continue the momentum. It is apparent that both sides see continued engagement at the highest level as key to sustaining this process of normalisation.

The dual tracks of the SR meetings and the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on border affairs, a body comprising diplomats and military officials, have worked well towards keeping the borders generally stable over the past two years. The latest outcomes will certainly help in keeping the peace. Less clear is how both sides intend to take up the task of border delimitation. Neither side has explained which parts of the border they plan to delimit, or whether they are reconsidering the 2005 agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles, under which the SRs were tasked with first agreeing a framework to settle the boundary. While both sides in Beijing reaffirmed the 2005 agreement, Article 10 of its text notes that it is only on the basis of the framework that both sides can delineate the boundary. Tangible progress on the border dispute must certainly be welcomed. However, agreements made without public visibility, notwithstanding their merit, may invite suspicion. As India and China continue negotiating their long-running boundary question, it is imperative that they bring their publics along.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the overall message of the passage?
options: While recent high-level talks between India and China have produced positive steps toward border stability, maintaining public transparency is essential for long-term progress.
The resolution of the India-China border dispute relies primarily on military commanders rather than diplomatic negotiations under the 2005 agreement.
India and China have fully settled their boundary disputes through an eight-point consensus establishing new hotline channels and river data protocols.
The primary obstacle to normalising India-China relations is the unwillingness of leadership to engage in top-level summit meetings.
questions.correct_answer: While recent high-level talks between India and China have produced positive steps toward border stability, maintaining public transparency is essential for long-term progress.
questions.explanation: The passage outlines the positive outcomes of recent high-level talks and mechanisms that keep borders stable, but concludes with the core warning that progress without public visibility invites suspicion, making public engagement imperative.

questions.question: Based on the passage facts that Article 10 of the 2005 agreement requires boundary delineation to build on an agreed framework, and that neither side has clarified whether such a framework exists, what can be inferred?
options: Boundary delineation cannot logically proceed under the 2005 agreement until both nations explicitly define and finalize the settlement framework.
The 2005 agreement has been officially rendered void by the new eight-point consensus reached during the Beijing talks.
Diplomats and military officials have abandoned Article 10 to expedite boundary agreements without public oversight.
The Special Representatives have resolved all framework ambiguities by setting up two new military hotline channels.
questions.correct_answer: Boundary delineation cannot logically proceed under the 2005 agreement until both nations explicitly define and finalize the settlement framework.
questions.explanation: Deducing from Fact 1 (Article 10 states delineation occurs only on the basis of the framework) and Fact 2 (neither side has clarified if they are reconsidering the 2005 framework agreement or explained which parts to delimit), it follows that delineation under these terms cannot move forward without establishing that foundational framework.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is directly contradicted by the passage?
options: The recent consensus explicitly specified the exact territorial segments along the border that both nations intend to delimit.
India has actively pushed for communication and data sharing regarding trans-border rivers.
The National Security Adviser’s visit to Beijing occurred prior to India hosting the BRICS Summit.
Two new channels of hotlines will be established in the Eastern and Middle Sectors.
questions.correct_answer: The recent consensus explicitly specified the exact territorial segments along the border that both nations intend to delimit.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph explicitly states: 'Neither side has explained which parts of the border they plan to delimit', directly contradicting the claim that specific territorial segments were specified.

questions.question: What is the author's primary intention in writing this passage?
options: To commend the tangible diplomatic progress made by India and China while emphasizing the necessity of public transparency.
To condemn both governments for keeping border negotiations completely secret from military leaders.
To argue that the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination is ineffective at maintaining border stability.
To demand an immediate suspension of top-level bilateral meetings until all boundary lines are fully mapped.
questions.correct_answer: To commend the tangible diplomatic progress made by India and China while emphasizing the necessity of public transparency.
questions.explanation: The author praises the 'tangible progress' and 'substantial outcomes' achieved through diplomacy, but highlights that agreements made without public visibility invite suspicion, intending to urge both sides to bring their publics along.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'early and substantial harvest' mean in the context of the passage?
options: Prompt and significant tangible outcomes achieved through diplomatic negotiations.
An accelerated agricultural yield along disputed river basin borders.
A rapid, unilateral withdrawal of military forces from frontline sectors.
The complete and final settlement of all historical territorial boundaries.
questions.correct_answer: Prompt and significant tangible outcomes achieved through diplomatic negotiations.
questions.explanation: In diplomatic negotiation context, 'harvest' refers to the positive, concrete yields or results achieved from talks, so an 'early and substantial harvest' means obtaining meaningful, tangible agreements quickly.

questions.question: According to the passage, what explicitly caused the borders between India and China to remain generally stable over the past two years?
options: The dual tracks of the Special Representatives meetings and the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination.
The immediate delineation of boundary sectors under Article 10 of the 2005 agreement.
The complete public disclosure of all confidential bilateral treaties in Beijing.
The arrival of President Xi Jinping in India after a seven-year gap.
questions.correct_answer: The dual tracks of the Special Representatives meetings and the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states in paragraph 2: 'The dual tracks of the SR meetings and the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on border affairs... have worked well towards keeping the borders generally stable over the past two years.'

questions.question: What evidence does the author present to support the claim that both sides view high-level engagement as key to sustaining normalization?
options: The progression of top-level interactions including the October 2024 Modi-Xi meeting, the 2025 Tianjin meeting, and the NSA's Beijing visit.
The refusal of both nations to discuss hydrological data sharing during expert-level meetings.
The absence of public announcements regarding border delimitation parameters.
The establishment of military hotline channels strictly limited to the Western Sector.
questions.correct_answer: The progression of top-level interactions including the October 2024 Modi-Xi meeting, the 2025 Tianjin meeting, and the NSA's Beijing visit.
questions.explanation: The author explicitly cites the October 2024 Modi-Xi meeting, the 2025 Tianjin meeting, and the NSA's Beijing visit before the BRICS summit as evidence showing both sides see engagement at the highest level as key to sustaining normalisation.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate contextual synonym for the word 'imperative' as used in the passage?
options: Essential
Optional
Uncertain
Secondary
questions.explanation: In the concluding sentence 'it is imperative that they bring their publics along', the word 'imperative' means crucial, vital, or absolutely essential.
